corrections.original: Glenn Fiedler's 'Fix Your Timestep!' (2004) is 'the canonical game-dev statement' and 'the game-programming article that named the spiral of death'.
corrections.fix: The article calls it 'the so called "spiral of death"', so it did not coin the term. Reworded to 'a widely cited article that discusses the so-called spiral of death'. Date Jun 10, 2004 and the quotes are confirmed verbatim.

corrections.original: Belief of the age: chenguini/index.ts hold the fixed-step-plus-cap belief; key claim 17 says Handwired snaps 'instead of carrying the backlog as chenguini's Animation.md recommends'.
corrections.fix: Since commit 2026-02-28 ('Docs: prefer closed-form animations over numerical stepping'), Animation.md has preferred closed-form springs (section 'Closed-Form vs Numerical': 'no catch-up loop, no accumulated integration drift, and no spiral-of-death cap'). Cap-and-carry (N = 300, 'no time skip') is its guidance for numerical springs only; the cap was added 2026-02-27. Dated timeline rows and nuance added; the claim that Handwired's snap departs from Animation.md's numerical-spring guidance still stands.

corrections.original: index.ts is grouped with the practice 'to prevent the spiral of death, cap the steps'.
corrections.fix: index.ts runs every pending step with no cap: line 408 has steps = Math.floor((now - newAnimatedUntilTime) / msPerAnimationStep) and no Math.min. host-timing.ts L123-L124 says the same. Nuance added.

corrections.original: In-program matrix power costs 546 operations for the frame matrix 'vs 14 for reading host-written cells (differentiability.md L5)'.
corrections.fix: differentiability.md L5 compares 546 with 119 ('when spring-bank writes the powers into weights'). The 14 is execution-model.md L178's cost for emitApplySpringMatrix, and L287 says source-matrix 'adds none' to the clock. Each number is now attributed to its own source.

corrections.original: Key claim 16: the older emitSpring with 4 in-program Euler steps is 46 operations in 33 layers.
corrections.fix: Re-measured 46 ops / 33 layers only when the parameters are declared nonnegative and unit is declared 1, as in costs.ts buildHandwiredOsSpring. With no declared ranges the same call compiles to 78 ops / 45 layers. Caveat added: say '46 operations in 33 layers, as HandwiredOS built it'.

corrections.original: Key claim 18: the chain rule gives -0.50469 for damping after 16 steps.
corrections.fix: The docs print -0.5047 (differentiability.md L271 and L281; tables-javascript-writes.md L52). The fifth digit comes only from an earlier report.ts run that this pass could not repeat. Use -0.5047 on screen. Stiffness 0.1055 is confirmed and pinned by test.

corrections.original: Damping gradients at n = 150 (-0.0011773) and n = 300 (-1.52e-6).
corrections.fix: These are in no doc (the differentiability.md L354-L360 table gives stiffness only, which matches) and report.ts could not be re-run. Marked unverifiable: do not show.

Recomputed with the real springStepMatrix and countSpringSteps: 533.4349, so 533.43. The other trajectory values are confirmed (412.26, 437.32, 468.51, 501.46, 569.71, 699.10, peak 700.317 at frame 26).
